subject: Intermittent throughput drop impacting Novado API - immediate attention
messages:
From: Claire Park <claire.park@novado.ai>
To: support@redwood.ai
Cc: Ops Team <ops@novado.ai>
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden throughput degradation on POST /v1/generate (affecting many customers)

Hi Redwood team —

We started seeing repeated 503s and long queuing delays on our calls to /v1/generate starting ~08:45 PT this morning. The success rate dropped from ~99.7% to ~86% and our throughput (requests/min) fell by ~40% despite request volume being steady. This is affecting multiple downstream customers and our alerts are firing.

What we've captured so far:
- Error sample: "503 Service Unavailable - backend_rejected"
- Latency spikes: p50 ~= 110ms (normal), p95 ~= 1.2s (up from 240ms)
- Notable pattern: many requests appear to be queued for >800ms before being forwarded.

We urgently need visibility on whether you're hitting concurrency caps, whether autoscale was delayed, or if there's a throttling/backoff loop on your side. Please escalate — our CS and engineering leads are looped.

Attached a short snippet of our client logs (novado_latency_log_snip.txt).

Thanks,
Claire
Head of Platform Reliability
Novado AI
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Park <claire.park@novado.ai>
Cc: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 09:27:14 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput degradation on POST /v1/generate (affecting many customers)

Claire — thanks for the heads up and for the log snippet. We're taking this as P1 and will investigate immediately. Short plan:

1) Internal triage (engineers on call) to confirm whether this is an internal concurrency cap/autoscaling symptom.
2) Share initial metrics (request rate, queued requests, worker utilization) within 20 minutes.
3) If it's Redwood-side capacity/queueing, we'll provision emergency burst capacity and open a canary fallback to a compatible model variant.

Markus and Dev — can you pick this up? I'll coordinate with Novado until we have a concrete mitigation.

Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 09:42:55 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput degradation on POST /v1/generate (affecting many customers)

On it. Quick notes from initial checks:
- Autoscaling did kick, but we observed a stretched scaling window between 08:40 and 09:05 where worker spin-up lagged behind request bursts.
- Concurrent active requests per worker spiked ~3x above baseline; concurrency caps were reached for several pools tied to us-west-2.
- The serving runtime's admission controller began rejecting new requests to preserve memory/kv cache integrity (hence the 503s).

Immediate mitigations applied at 09:35:
- Increased concurrency cap temporarily for the affected pools.
- Triggered on-demand hotpool nodes (provisioned additional GPUs) to soak backlog.
- Enabled a model-variant fallback (1.3B quantized) for non-critical customer routes to reduce per-request GPU memory.

We pushed metrics (redwood_metrics_20261005.csv) to the shared drive and are closely watching p50/p95/p99. Dev to follow up with logs.

— Markus
VP, Site Reliability
From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Claire Park <claire.park@novado.ai>
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 10:11:02 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput degradation on POST /v1/generate (affecting many customers)

Claire and Novado ops — following up with a few more technical details from our side:

- Root cause hypothesis: a client-side request pattern from one of Novado's internal batch jobs created high concurrency on a subset of keys causing KV cache pressure and longer per-request scheduling time. The combination of cache pressure + the admission controller tripping produced the long queue times.
- We have a short-term config change: reduce per-request max tokens for Novado's account for the next 2 hours and route bulk/batch work to a dedicated dedicated-batch pool. This will limit concurrent memory usage per worker.
- Longer term: we recommend pinning heavier batch workloads to Redwood Dedicated or Private with guarantees on concurrency and reserved GPU counts.

Action items we took at 10:05:
- Applied per-customer token cap and created a temporary dedicated-batch pool for Novado.
- Cleared backlog; success rates climbed back to ~98% by ~10:20 with p95 dropping to ~300ms for most routes.

I'll continue to monitor; attaching the log slice showing admission controller hits.

— Dev
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Park <claire.park@novado.ai>
Cc: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent throughput degradation on POST /v1/generate - postmortem and next steps

Claire — following up with a brief post-incident summary and next steps. Thanks for your patience and for surfacing this quickly.

Summary:
- Incident window: 2026-10-03 08:45 PT to 2026-10-03 10:25 PT.
- Impact: transient 503s and elevated queuing caused Novado's success rate to dip to ~86% at peak.
- Immediate cause: a burst of high-concurrency batch traffic created KV cache pressure; admission controller rejected new work when per-pool concurrency caps were exceeded and autoscaling lagged during the burst.

What we did to remediate:
- Temporarily increased concurrency caps and provisioned hotpool capacity (reduced queueing within ~30 minutes).
- Routed bulk batch traffic to a temporary dedicated pool and applied a per-request token cap for Novado.
- Rolled a model-variant fallback for non-critical routes to reduce per-request memory pressure.

Follow-up actions (timeline):
1) By Oct 9: Engineering will tune admission controller thresholds and reduce scale-up latency (jonas_weber + dev_patel).
2) By Oct 12: SRE and Accounts to propose recommended traffic-pattern knobs for Novado (reserved burst capacity, token caps, dedicated-batch pool) and a short-runbook for their ops team (markus_klein + karthik_iyer).
3) By Oct 19: Consider Dedicated plan trial for Novado (performance SLA, reserved concurrency) — Sales to present commercial options (karthik_iyer).

Attached: redwood_metrics_20261005.csv (metrics snapshot), novado_latency_log_snip.txt (client logs).

If Novado would like a technical deep-dive meeting, we can schedule a 30–45 minute session next week to walk the SREs through the admission controller behavior and the recommended traffic patterns.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
